entries.notes: Theorem 3.8 (l.337) and Theorem C.1 (l.880) now carry the same sentence: TV(mu||nu) := 1/2 ||mu - nu|| = sup_A |mu(A) - nu(A)|, the total variation distance between probability measures, with ||mu - nu|| := (mu - nu)^+(S) + (mu - nu)^-(S) and A over the measurable subsets, followed by '(the bound is attained on a two-point example)'. Lean defines EGF.tvDist mu nu := tvMass mu nu / 2 (Sampling.lean:486) and tvMass := (mu - nu)(S) + (nu - mu)(S) (Universality.lean:104). These are Mathlib's truncated differences, which for finite measures are the Jordan parts of the signed measure mu - nu (Measure.toJordanDecomposition_toSignedMeasure_sub, the identification terminalError_eq_posPart uses), so ||.|| is tvMass literally. EGF.tvDist_eq_iSup gives the sup form under equal masses, which 'between probability measures' supplies. Its (mu A - nu A) sup (nu A - mu A) in [0, inf] is |mu(A) - nu(A)| for finite values. The restriction to probability measures restricts nothing in either theorem, since both arguments are probability measures. The law of s_tau is one by main_quantitative_sampling clause 3, given tau < inf a.s. (clause 1). F-hat_term/F-hat_term(S) is one because F-hat_term(S) = F_init(S) + dF_init(S) > 0 (clause 4). Hypotheses: Theorem 3.8 takes a generative flow, finite F_init and F_term, and F_init != 0. main_quantitative_sampling takes F : GenerativeFlow, [IsFiniteMeasure] and hinit, with no flow matching. They match. The conclusion is clause 5, weaker than the anchor. 'Attained on a two-point example' is clause 1 of EGF.TwoPoint.negative_control_sharp: S = Bool, pi = id, F_out = 0, F_init = delta_true, F_term = delta_false, giving TV = 1/2 = dF_init(S)/F-hat_term(S). That instance meets every hypothesis. Refutation: there the unhalved norm is 1 > 1/2 (clause 2). With the 1/2 the instance meets the bound with equality, so it refutes nothing. The other TV uses are in the 1/2 convention and consistent: l.342, l.347, l.353 (1/2 sum |.|), l.356, and Pinsker at l.393 with sqrt(1/2 KL). added_hypotheses = [] and none was added: 'between probability measures' scopes the definition, not the theorem. The applied text elaborates the register's corrected (finding 7).

l.889, in the proof of Theorem C.1, after the F' sentence: 'The sampler of F from F_init thus terminates almost surely, with E tau <= (F-hat_term(S) + F_out*(S))/F_init(S), since F_init <= F-hat_init and F' is flow matching from F-hat_init (Theorem 2.1); in particular s_tau is well defined.' This matches main_quantitative_sampling clauses 1-3. Clause 1 is pathLaw F_init F-hat {stopTime = top} = 0. Clause 2 is lintegral of stopTime <= (F-hat(S) + F_out(S))/F_init(S), the same bound. Clause 3 says the law of sampledState is a probability measure, which is 'well defined'. The hypotheses are C.1's: F_init != 0, finite measures, no flow matching. The justification is sound. The unnormalised occupation is monotone in the initial measure, so F_init(S) E tau <= F-hat_init(S)(F_out(S)/F-hat_init(S) + 1) = F_out(S) + F-hat_term(S), by Theorem 2.1's mass identity. The Lean proof is the super-solution form of the same argument: occupation_le with finit_super, from isFlowMatching_virtual. Kind gap, so there is no refutation. added_hypotheses = [] and none was added.

There are two edits. Edit (i), l.167: 'The stopping decision at time t depends only on s_1, ..., s_t and an independent coin (a randomized stopping time).' Edit (ii), l.189: Theorem 2.1 adds 'tau < inf almost surely' to its conclusion. Edit (ii) is EGF.sampling_theorem clause 3 (pathLaw {stopTime = top} = 0). The other conclusions match one for one: F_init(S) = F_term(S); lintegral tau <= F_out(S)/F_init(S) + 1; map sampledState = normalize F_term, which is 's_tau ~ F_term' read through l.159. So do the hypotheses: finite F_init and F_term; F_term != 0; GenerativeFlow; IsFlowMatching (l.186). Edit (i) is finding 1. EGF.sampling_theorem is a statement about one measure, GenerativeFlow.pathLaw. Its transition pathKernel (Sampling.lean:785) draws y ~ pi(x) whatever the flag and raises a lowered flag at y with probability stop(y), by a fresh coin. In words: given tau >= t and the whole past, the sampler stops at t with probability stop(s_t), and the decision reads only s_t and an independent coin. That is one member of the class the TeX now describes. The TeX lets the decision read s_1..s_t, and its hazard P(tau = t | tau >= t) = h(s_t) does not say what it conditions on. Read as conditioned on (tau >= t, s_t), which is all pathLaw_spec clause 4 states, the class contains history-dependent randomized stopping times whose joint law differs from pathLaw's. The theorem is true on that class. The stopping-time property and the coin's independence give P(tau >= t+1, s_{t+1} in .) = ((1 - h) P(tau >= t, s_t in .)) pi, which is the recursion of GenerativeFlow.occ. So the law of (tau, s_tau) is pathLaw's, and a version h is harmless because the super-solution (F_term + F_out)/F_init(S) works for every version. But no declaration of lean-egf states a sampling theorem over a class of stopping times, or that every member of the class has pathLaw's law (grep: 'randomized' occurs only in docstrings). EGF.sampling_theorem therefore covers the Markov instance only, and the TeX claims more. Read as conditioned on the past, the class has a single joint law, pathLaw's. That is the reading the T-egf-sampling audit checked by reading the definition ('both natural conditionings, on the past and on the whole trajectory, give pathLaw's law'), but the TeX does not say it. Theorems 3.8 and C.1 and Corollary 3.9 inherit the issue, since they use the same sampler. added_hypotheses ('the stopping rule is a randomized stopping time') is at l.167, and nothing else was added, so hypotheses_ok holds; but the listed hypothesis names the class, which is wider than the anchor's model. Kind missing-hypothesis, so there is no refutation declaration. The finding's look-ahead instance (a decision reading s_{t+1}: 2/3 instead of 1/2 on the audit's {a, b} flow) is excluded by l.167, and would also be excluded by either fix below. 'tau in N_{>=1}' at l.165 is left inconsistent with edit (ii) (finding 3).

The l.165 footnote now reads: 'Clearly F_term << F_term + F_out* so the Radon-Nikodym derivative is well-defined, up to a (F_term + F_out*)-null set; under the flow-matching constraint (2) the chain's unstopped mass sum_{t>=1} P(tau >= t, s_t in .) is dominated by (F_term + F_out*)/F_init(S), so the law of the sampler does not depend on the version chosen.' Clause by clause: (a) 'F_term << G', with G = F_term + F_out, is fterm_ac_stopBase. (b) 'Up to a null set' holds because the Radon-Nikodym derivative is an a.e. class. (c) The unstopped mass is GenerativeFlow.occupation F_term (normalize F_init) = sum_n occ_n, with occ_n = P(tau >= n+1, s_{n+1} in .) (the hocc step of pathLaw_spec), so the TeX's sum is the Lean's. (d) 'Dominated by': under flow matching, occupation_ac_of_isFlowMatching gives << G (the paper's l.157 sense), and occupation_le with normalize_add_step gives <= G/F_init(S), so both readings are proved. (e) The conclusion 'the law of the sampler does not depend on the version chosen' is not what the anchors prove (finding 2). pathLaw has no version parameter: it is built from the one version stop = 1 - min(dF_out/dG, 1). pathLaw_hazard_rnDeriv proves that this sampler also satisfies the hazard with Mathlib's rnDeriv wherever its unstopped mass is << G, i.e. one law obeys the hazard for two versions. No sampler is built from another version h and compared with pathLaw. The corrector's argument is correct mathematics: two G-a.e. equal versions give the same path law, since the unstopped mass charges no G-null set and a raised flag reads no version. But that is not a kernel-checked statement. The T-egf-sampling audit (AUDIT-1, minor finding 2) said the same of the REPORT's 'so every version gives the same sampler law', which the footnote now carries into the paper. added_hypotheses = [] and none was added ('under the flow-matching constraint' qualifies the remark and is in corrected). Kind gap, so there is no refutation.

l.891: 'If dF_init(S) = 0, then F-hat_init = F_init, F is flow matching from F_init to F-hat_term and the bound, 0, is Theorem 2.1; assume dF_init(S) > 0.' This is correct. dF_init(S) = 0 forces dF_init = 0 and F-hat_init = F_init. isFlowMatching_virtual gives flow matching from F_init to F-hat_term. Theorem 2.1 needs F-hat_term != 0, which l.887 has just shown. Then s_tau ~ F-hat_term and TV = 0, which is the bound. The anchor EGF.normalize_add_sub_normalize_le (a != 0, b finite: normalize(a+b) - normalize a <= ((a+b)(S))^{-1} b, setwise) needs no case split, since b = dF_init may vanish. The TeX's split is therefore a proof route that the anchor makes unnecessary, not a hypothesis, and the case lies inside main_quantitative_sampling anyway. It is placed before the mixture identity (after v1 l.857, before v1 l.858), as corrected says. added_hypotheses = [] and none was added. Kind gap.

l.346-348 adds a proof of Corollary 3.9. Step by step against SamplingCorollaries.lean: (a) 'at F_term = kappa-hat the terminal error vanishes' is terminalError_kappaHat; (b) 'F-hat_term = kappa-hat' is virtualTerm_kappaHat; (c) 'dF_init = (F_init + F_in - F_out)^-' is initialError_kappaHat, with inferenceDefect the negative part (inferenceDefect_eq_negPart); (d) 'F-hat_term(S) = 1 + delta' is main_quantitative_sampling clause 4 at F_init(S) = 1, i.e. sampling_error_control clause 3; (e) 'Theorem 3.8 gives TV(s_tau || kappa-hat/kappa-hat(S)) <= delta/(1+delta)' is sampling_error_control clause 4; (f) 'the triangle inequality for TV concludes' is EGF.tvDist_triangle, giving clause 5. All three TV arguments are probability measures (s_tau; kappa-hat/kappa-hat(S), with kappa-hat(S) = 1 + delta >= 1; kappa/kappa(S)), so C-11's 'between probability measures' covers them. 'The bound holds for every generative flow and every finite kappa != 0' is checked as follows. sampling_error_control takes F : GenerativeFlow (any flow), [IsProbabilityMeasure F_init] (the statement's F_init(S) = 1) and [IsFiniteMeasure kappa]. Lean allows kappa = 0 only through the junk value normalize 0 = 0, while the TeX's kappa/kappa(S) is undefined there. So kappa != 0 is the TeX's presupposition, not a restriction, and is not a finding. 'Trained on the target kappa' stays as context, which the proof's last sentence makes explicit. added_hypotheses = [] and none was added. Kind gap.

findings.what: C-13 (point 1). EGF.sampling_theorem covers only the Markov instance. Its sampler, GenerativeFlow.pathLaw (pathKernel), stops at time t with probability stop(s_t) given tau >= t and the whole past, by a fresh coin. The edited TeX instead admits any stopping decision that 'depends only on s_1..s_t and an independent coin', and its hazard P(tau = t | tau >= t) = dF_term/d(F_term+F_out*)(s_t) does not say what it conditions on. Read as conditioned on (tau >= t, s_t), which is exactly what pathLaw_spec clause 4 checks, this is a class of history-dependent randomized stopping times with different joint laws. The theorem's conclusions do hold on that class: the unstopped marginals satisfy GenerativeFlow.occ's recursion, so the law of (tau, s_tau) is pathLaw's. But no Lean declaration states this. So Theorem 2.1, and through the same sampler Theorems 3.8 and C.1 and Corollary 3.9, claim more than their anchors. Read as conditioned on the past, the class collapses to pathLaw's law, which is the reading the T-egf-sampling audit checked by reading pathKernel; the TeX does not say that.
findings.fix: TeX, inside C-13's printed range (l.163-165), with either of two wordings. (a) Condition the hazard on the past: '$\mathbb P(\tau = t\mid\tau\geq t,\underline s_1,\dots,\underline s_t) = \frac{d\Fterm}{d(\Fterm+\Foutstar)}(\underline s_t)$', with l.167 reading 'The stopping decision at time $t$ reads only $\underline s_1,\dots,\underline s_t$ and a coin independent of the chain, which moves on by $\ForwardPolicyStar$ regardless (a randomized stopping time).' (b) The instance wording: 'At each time $t$ with $\tau\geq t$ the sampler stops with probability $\frac{d\Fterm}{d(\Fterm+\Foutstar)}(\underline s_t)$, by a coin independent of the chain and of the earlier coins; the chain moves on by $\ForwardPolicyStar$ regardless, so $\tau$ is a randomized stopping time.' Both describe pathLaw, and both stay within OQ-60 (b) as DEC-141 ruled it (the decision reads only the past and an independent coin, and the chain moves on by pi regardless). The ruling confirmed the reading the marks rest on. It does not require the TeX to state the wider class, and DEC-141 adopts the smallest correction proved sufficient. Then update C-13's corrected and added_hypotheses to match. Alternative that keeps the TeX: prove in lean-egf a sampling theorem over any probability space carrying a pi-chain (s_t), a coin U independent of it, and a stopping time tau of sigma(s_1..s_t, U) with P(tau = t, s_t in A) = int_A h dP(tau >= t, s_t in .). Its unstopped marginals satisfy the occ recursion, which yields sampling_theorem's conclusions (and main_quantitative_sampling's for F-hat_term).

findings.what: C-14 (point 2). The footnote ends with 'so the law of the sampler does not depend on the version chosen', and its anchors do not prove that. pathLaw is built from one fixed version, stop = 1 - min(dF_out/dG, 1) with G = F_term + F_out, and has no version parameter. pathLaw_hazard_rnDeriv shows that this one sampler also satisfies the hazard with Mathlib's rnDeriv wherever its unstopped mass is << G. occupation_ac_of_isFlowMatching supplies that domination under flow matching. No sampler is built from another G-a.e. version h and compared with pathLaw. The corrector's argument is correct: two G-a.e. equal versions give the same path law, because the unstopped mass charges no G-null set and a raised flag reads no version. It is still not a kernel-checked statement. The T-egf-sampling audit (AUDIT-1, minor finding 2) flagged the same sentence in the REPORT ('so every version gives the same sampler law'). Earlier clauses of the footnote are proved: F_term << G (fterm_ac_stopBase); the unstopped mass is sum_n occ_n, with occ_n = P(tau >= n+1, s_{n+1} in .); and the domination is both << (the anchor) and <= G/F_init(S) (occupation_le with normalize_add_step).
findings.fix: TeX, the wording the audit proposed: '... is dominated by $(\Fterm+\Foutstar)/\Finit(\Statespace)$, so it charges no $(\Fterm+\Foutstar)$-null set, and the sampler obeys the hazard above for every version.' That is pathLaw_hazard_rnDeriv with its integrand changed on an occupation-null set (one setLIntegral_congr_fun_ae step), and ideally also stated as a lemma, pathLaw_hazard_of_ae_eq. Alternatively, in Lean: build the sampler from any measurable h with values in [0,1] and prove that two (F_term + F_out)-a.e. equal choices give the same pathLaw under flow matching (induct on occ, which is << G). Then the footnote stands, with that lemma added to C-14's anchor.

findings.what: C-13 / C-12 (point 6). l.165 still defines 'the sampling time tau in N_{>=1}'. The batch now concludes 'tau < inf almost surely' in Theorem 2.1 (l.189) and proves 'the sampler ... terminates almost surely' in C.1's proof (l.889). Both are vacuous for an N_{>=1}-valued tau. Worse, the definition presupposes the termination that C-13's finding says must be proved ('s_tau ~ F_term presupposes tau < inf a.s.'). For a general flow, e.g. one whose stopping probability vanishes, no N_{>=1}-valued tau has the hazard at all. Lean's time is stopTime : N-infinity (Sampling.lean:1072), with {stopTime = top} a null event only under the theorems' hypotheses. This line is inside C-13's printed range (163-165) and within the substance of its finding, so it falls under C-13's scope. It was left because C-13's corrected text does not name it.
findings.fix: Amend C-13's corrected text to include l.164 (v1) '$\tau \in \mathbb N_{\geq 1}\cup\{\infty\}$', optionally adding 's_tau on {tau < inf}'. Then apply it with an EGF-C13 marker.

findings.what: C-17 (point 6). '(\ForwardPolicyStar,\foutstar)' remains in the remark between Definition 3.7 and Theorem 3.8 (l.329, v1 l.320) and in Theorem C.1 (l.876, v1 l.846).
